findings.title: the production five-hour launcher did not classify SUPERVISOR_START_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE as a supervisor-acknowledgment failure, so a start-identity refusal was recorded as SUPERVISOR_SPAWN_FAILED
findings.authority_impact: NONE. The governed transfer was already fail-closed: ok === false, nothing launched, the capability TRANSFERRED_SPENT, a retry refused ALREADY_TRANSFERRED, the private key deleted, buffers zeroed, the descriptor closed, the child killed and reaped, and zero provider spawns. No forged start identity was ever accepted. The defect could not produce a false success and could not weaken any authority control.
findings.what_was_false: The recorded final_state 'SUPERVISOR_SPAWN_FAILED' and stage 'governed_key_transfer' state that the spawn/key-transfer stage failed. In the SUPERVISOR_START_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE scenario the process spawn SUCCEEDED, the one-use inherited-descriptor key transfer COMPLETED, and the spawned supervisor really did mint a CORRECTLY EPHEMERAL-SIGNED claim bound to the exact spawned PID. The only thing that failed was the parent's INDEPENDENT /bin/ps observation of the process-start identity — an acknowledgment-stage failure. A founder reading that run record would have drawn a materially wrong conclusion about what happened.
findings.mechanism_confirmed: FG-FFIN4-197-01 added a FOURTH acknowledgment-stage lifecycle code to src/v8b/lrcq/assurance/lifecycle-authority-v4.mjs (declared at :55, returned from awaitVerifiedSupervisorClaim at :595). The launcher's classification was an inline three-code OR expression that was not extended, and the following line is a pure ternary on that boolean, so the new code fell to the else arm. This is the same defect CLASS the lane already corrected once as FG-FFIN-197-F1, whose stated purpose was that 'the refusal state is named after the actual failure so the evidence record cannot describe a claim failure as a spawn failure'. The existing regression that governs refusal-stage naming (detached-supervisor-failure case 10b) asserted it for the other three codes only, so nothing caught the drift.

reproduction_of_the_false_classification.method: DYNAMIC. The `const claimFailure = ...;` expression was extracted VERBATIM from the pre-correction tools/terminal0/lrcq/run-five-hour.mjs with a regex, compiled with new Function('g','LC_CODES', ...), and evaluated against every acknowledgment-stage code the authority module can return. This executed the real production predicate rather than a paraphrase of it.
reproduction_of_the_false_classification.reachability_of_the_code: Independently proven by the fifth Checker: under genuine external OS file-descriptor exhaustion (no production hook, no flag, no substitute executable) spawnGovernedSupervisorV4 returns { ok:false, code:'SUPERVISOR_START_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE' } — reproduced at fd headroom 2, 3 and 4 plus a 30s sustained-failure run, each with the child's correctly signed claim on disk and claim.supervisor_pid === the spawned pid.
